negative_cases.foreign_workstream: validate_scope validates the projection WorkstreamKey and rejects a foreign expected Workstream. A focused WorkSurface also requires an exact Attachment-backed WorkSurfaceId, and nested eligible contribution authority cannot carry a foreign Workstream into the projection.
negative_cases.missing_authority: The generated flattened projection requires WorkstreamKey during deserialization; missing or legacy-only projection input fails closed. An eligible contribution without a generated workstream authority descriptor is rejected.
negative_cases.stale_revision_cursor: Projection revision and durable event cursor remain required generated projection fields and are preserved through serialization; stale revision/cursor mutation remains owned by reducer/persistence optimistic-concurrency gates rather than inferred by client code.
negative_cases.unavailable_capability: validate_scope does not resolve or suspend contributions. Capability, permission, operation, meaningful-content, and omission decisions remain in the core resolver and are not recreated in the projection model.
negative_cases.ineligible_or_empty_contribution: The projection scope validator does not promote empty or ineligible contributions and does not calculate layout. Core eligibility/layout continue to omit them before geometry; a Workstream aggregate can validate attachment-owned contributions without guessing a single focus.
negative_cases.ambiguous_legacy_row: A projection serialized without WorkstreamKey cannot deserialize as ResolvedWorkspaceProjection. No project_root plus continuity_id fallback, current-tab lookup, or nearest-row inference was added; legacy compatibility remains a separate quarantine boundary.
